blocks.text: Walk the environment layer by layer, confirming each before moving on; every step rules out a whole class of bugs.

items: Right code? Stale image (no `--build`), wrong tag: `docker compose images`, `cat` the file inside.
Right command and WORKDIR? `docker inspect` Entrypoint/Cmd/WorkingDir.
Env present? `docker compose exec api printenv`; your laptop's .env isn't in the image.
Files present? .dockerignore exclusions, bind mounts hiding content, files outside the context.
Case sensitivity: macOS is case-insensitive, Linux isn't (`import Utils` vs utils.py).
Network: localhost = container; use service:containerPort; bind 0.0.0.0.
Permissions: non-root vs root-owned dirs, volume ownership, `--read-only` blocking cwd/$HOME writes.
OS libs: libpq5, libgomp1, libGL, ca-certificates, tzdata, locales, musl vs glibc.
Resources: memory limit, /dev/shm size, CPU throttling, worker auto-sizing.
Timing: dependencies not ready, no retries.
Time/locale: UTC, missing LANG → encoding errors.

blocks.text:
$ docker compose exec api sh -c 'id; pwd; ls -la; python -V; printenv | sort | cut -c1-60'
$ docker compose exec api python -c "import app.main"     # surfaces import and .so errors

Q: "It works on my machine but not in Docker. How do you approach it?" A: "Methodically: confirm the image and code actually running, then platform, command and working directory, env, files, network addressing, permissions, OS libraries, resource limits and timing, testing each from inside the container."

items: Most failures: env, network addressing, permissions, OS libs.
